title: Report
description: Final structured report — only reachable, deduped findings.

variants.description: Other findings in the same dedupe group ('Also at:'). The report agent's own output (validated here BEFORE report.py's post-hoc attach overwrites this field) may carry bare finding_id strings; the final, authoritative form report.py attaches from run state is a located object: {finding_id, file, line_start, line_end, vuln_class}.

cvss.description: CVSS 3.1 base score/severity/vector for this finding. The report agent is expected to emit a real vector (matching validate's cvss_vector when the finding was confirmed with one); report.py's _attach_cvss backfills a severity-keyed baseline for whatever is left unset and never overwrites an existing value.

impact.description: What an attacker actually gains, or what breaks, if this is exploited.

exploit_scenario.description: Concrete narrative: how an attacker with the access described in `trace.entry_points` reaches and triggers this.

preconditions.description: Conditions that must hold for the exploit to work (auth level, feature flag, network position). Empty if none.

how_to_fix.description: Concrete remediation — the specific function/API/validation to change. A more detailed companion to `recommendation`.

validation.description: Adversarial-verification outcome for this finding — Validate's verdict/rationale/validator_confidence. Injected from the run state (Finding.validation_status/validation_json) by report.py's _attach_validation; never agent-authored (Validate runs before Report and CANNOT emit new findings, so this is only ever a read of its already-stored verdict). Only the keys Validate actually emitted are present.

confidence.description: The hunter's own confidence in the finding (distinct from `validation.validator_confidence`). Injected from the run state (Finding.confidence) by report.py's _attach_validation.

chains.description: Multi-step exploit chains (V11) — combinations of >=2 findings more dangerous than any single bug. Each chain carries its OWN severity; per-finding severities are unchanged (CVSS/V4 stays authoritative). Injected from the run state by report.py.

input_inventory.description: Resolved completeness ledger — every attacker-controllable input Recon enumerated, each with its reconciled disposition (covered|uncovered). Injected from the run state by report.py; a completeness artifact, not a per-finding record.

coverage.description: Consolidated coverage disclosure (4.7). Merges the F1 input ledger, the 4.3 run_summary tasks/findings breakdowns, and the F6 catch-all sweep/drop counts into one object so an operator sees, in one place, what was and wasn't covered. Injected from the run state by report.py — optional and permissive (additionalProperties allowed) so it never blocks report emission or a future field addition.

tasks_by_source.description: Task count keyed by source (recon, catchall, reconcile, ...).

findings_by_status.description: Finding count keyed by validation_status (confirmed, false_positive, null=unvalidated, ...).

source_files.description: Eligible source files seen by the F6 catch-all sweep.

covered_files.description: Of source_files, how many were already targeted by some task before the sweep.

catchall_dropped.description: Eligible files the sweep could NOT queue because build_catchall_tasks's max_tasks cap was hit — coverage is INCOMPLETE whenever this is > 0.

coverage_complete.description: False when catchall_dropped > 0 or any enumerated input never reached a disposition. Never imply full coverage when this is false.

threat_model.description: Lightweight system threat model synthesized by the report agent from the recon context and findings already in its input (not fresh analysis). Optional — omitted when there is too little context to synthesize one responsibly.

system_context.description: Plain-language description of what the system does and how it is exposed.

assets.description: Things worth protecting that the findings touch (data, credentials, internal services).

trust_boundaries.description: Points where trust level changes that the findings actually cross (network edge, auth boundary, process boundary).

ranked_threats.description: The findings grouped into threats and ranked by how much each matters for this system.

open_questions.description: Things the agent could not resolve from recon + findings alone (needs a human, or more scanning).

scan_metrics.description: Run-level scan metrics — file coverage, duration, cost, and per-phase token usage. Injected from the run state by report.py (cost/coverage/duration are never agent-authored); each property is independently optional so a metric that isn't knowable yet (e.g. duration before the run finishes) is simply omitted rather than emitted as a misleading null.

tokens_by_phase.description: Token/cost aggregates per pipeline stage, from the costs table (db.run_summary).

verification.description: Verification funnel tally (raw hunter findings -> validated true/false positives), disclosing precision rather than just the final reachable/deduped `findings` count. Injected from the run state by report.py — authoritative, never agent-authored.
